correctness.rationale: The universal proof chooses coordinates with off-surface canonical point as the last basis vector and its square polar as the last coordinate. The normal form C+u²M+u³ is exact. Hessian alternating rank two gives rank 0 precisely on u=0, rank 2 off it; the plane cubic is smooth and ordinary. In local smooth coordinates, both columns of dGauss are divisible by u², and the two divided columns are linearly independent along u=0. This proves the maximal-minor ideal equals (u⁴) at every point of R and is the unit ideal off R. The standalone script additionally checks point ranks over GF(2),GF(4),GF(8) and one exact nonzero order-four minor; finite testing is not used to infer the general theorem.

value.rationale: The exact order-four scheme globally identifies nonordinary wild Gauss-differential ramification in a classical three-parameter regime of smooth cubic surfaces in characteristic two, sharply beyond the reduced canonical plane and its known Hessian null vector. The smooth ordinary critical plane cubic is natural, and the uniform Cartier quadrupling describes a nontrivial scheme-theoretic degeneracy invariant with potential use in dual geometry and positive-characteristic deformation arguments.
